drawings.notes: Panel labelled [图 3]. It is an NMR spectrum: a single trace with a chemical-shift axis running 9.0 down to 0.0, axis caption 'f1 (ppm)', i.e. a 1H NMR. Visible peaks near ~7.4 and ~7.25 (aromatic) and a very tall peak near ~2.5, with small satellites. No integrals or peak-value labels are printed, so no shift values are transcribed as data. The structure is an inset identifying the sample, not a reaction. Substituent labels read Br, Cl, CH3 and S-CH3; the top label is two characters, a rounded 'C' followed by a tall thin stroke, read as 'Cl' - the scan is degraded there, hence medium confidence on that atom. Positions above are read off the drawing geometry only.

drawings.notes: Panel labelled [图 4]. NMR spectrum with a chemical-shift axis running 170 down to 0, axis caption 'f1 (ppm)', i.e. a 13C NMR. Peaks appear roughly in the 120-140 region (several), a cluster near ~77 (solvent), and two tall peaks near ~20-25. No numeric peak labels are printed. Same inset structure as [图 3], drawn identically.

illegible: Top substituent label on both inset structures ([图 3] and [图 4]): a rounded glyph plus a tall thin stroke, most consistent with 'Cl' but the scan is broken up at that size. Read as Cl with medium confidence.
Chemical-shift axis tick numerals on both spectra are heavily degraded; they are legible only as an approximate scale (9.0-0.0 for [图 3], 170-0 for [图 4]) and individual digits cannot be guaranteed.
No peak-position or integral annotations are printed on either spectrum, so no shift values are recoverable from this page.
